title: Algebraic extension and restriction of valuation coarsenings
statement: Let $K\subseteq L$ be a finite algebraic extension of fields [def-pc-field-extension], and let $W\subseteq L$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $L$ [def-trf-valuation-ring]. Put $V=W\cap K$, a valuation ring of $K$. In additive notation let $w:L^\times\to\Gamma_W=L^\times/W^\times$ be its surjective valuation and identify $\Gamma_V=w(K^\times)$ with an ordered subgroup of $\Gamma_W$. Then $\Gamma_W/\Gamma_V$ is torsion: for every $\delta\in\Gamma_W$ there is an integer $n>0$ with $n\delta\in\Gamma_V$. Restriction $W'\mapsto W'\cap K$ is an inclusion-preserving bijection from the valuation rings $W\subseteq W'\subseteq L$ onto the valuation rings $V\subseteq V'\subseteq K$. Moreover $W'=L$ if and only if its restriction is $K$; in particular every proper valuation overring of $V$ lifts to a proper valuation overring of $W$. Here a valuation overring is a valuation ring in the same fraction field containing the indicated ring. No henselian or separability hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Restriction preserves the inverse alternative of [def-trf-valuation-ring]: for $x\in K^\times$, either $x\in W\cap K$ or $x^{-1}\in W\cap K$. Thus $V$ and every $W'\cap K$ are valuation rings of $K$; the same alternative writes each nonzero $x$ as a fraction of their elements. Also $K^\times\cap W^\times=V^\times$, since a unit is exactly an element whose inverse is in the ring. Hence $K^\times/V^\times$ identifies with $w(K^\times)$, preserving order because $b/a\in W$ for $a,b\in K^\times$ is equivalent to $b/a\in V$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-valuation-value-group-torsion] to $K\subseteq L$ and the subring $W$. Its hypotheses hold because the extension is algebraic and $W$ satisfies the inverse alternative. For each $x\in L^\times$ obtain $n\geq1$, $a\in K^\times$ and $u\in W^\times$ with $x^n=au$. Taking classes gives $n w(x)=w(a)\in\Gamma_V$. Surjectivity of $w$ proves the asserted torsion property.

proof.text: For an overring $V'\supseteq V$ put $S(V')=\{s\in V\setminus\{0\}:s^{-1}\in V'\}$ and $B(V')=\{y/s:y\in W,\ s\in S(V')\}\subseteq L$. The set $S(V')$ contains $1$ and is multiplicatively closed. These fractions form a subring: $(y/s)+(z/t)=(yt+zs)/(st)$, $(y/s)(z/t)=yz/(st)$, and $-(y/s)=(-y)/s$. It contains $W$ by denominator $1$, so the inverse alternative in $W$ implies it for $B(V')$; its fraction field is $L$ because it contains $W$. Thus [def-trf-valuation-ring] makes $B(V')$ a valuation overring of $W$.

proof.text: We have $B(V')\cap K=V'$. If $x=y/s\in B(V')\cap K$, then $y=sx\in W\cap K=V$, so $x=y s^{-1}\in V'$. Conversely $0\in B(V')$; for $x\in V'\setminus\{0\}$, if $x\in V$ use $x=x/1$. Otherwise [def-trf-valuation-ring] gives $s=x^{-1}\in V$, and $s^{-1}=x\in V'$, so $s\in S(V')$ and $x=1/s\in B(V')$.

proof.text: Restriction reflects inclusion among overrings of $W$. Suppose $W\subseteq U,T$ and $U\cap K\subseteq T\cap K$. For nonzero $x\in U$, [lem-trf-valuation-value-group-torsion] gives $x^n=au$ with $n>0$, $a\in K^\times$, and $u,u^{-1}\in W$. Thus $a=x^nu^{-1}\in U\cap K\subseteq T\cap K$, whence $x^n=au\in T$. A valuation subring is closed under positive roots: $v_T(x)^n\leq1$ implies $v_T(x)\leq1$ in its linearly ordered value group with zero. Therefore $x\in T$. Zero belongs to every subring. In particular restriction is injective. This replaces the explicit fraction calculation for uniqueness in the original plan.

proof.text: Steps 3–4 give a lift of every overring downstairs, so restriction is surjective. Step 5 gives injectivity and reflection of inclusion; restriction itself preserves inclusion directly. Its bijection is therefore an order isomorphism. The top overring $L$ restricts to $K$, and injectivity makes it the only overring with that restriction. For a proper overring $R$ downstairs, apply the inverse order isomorphism to obtain an overring $U$ of $W$ with restriction $R$; the top equivalence implies $U\ne L$.
